newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea's LPMO buys 8,095 tonnes of frozen beef.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea's LPMO buys 8,095 tonnes of frozen beef.

text.p: South Korea's state-run Livestock Products Marketing Organization (LPMO) said on Friday it had bought a total of 8,095 tonnes of frozen beef through tenders on June 27.
An official with the organisation said it had purchased 3,041 tonnes of U.S. beef, 288 tonnes of Canadian beef, 4,274 tonnes of Australian beef and 492 tonnes of New Zealand beef.

U.S. and Canadian chuck roll was bought at a range of $2,546-$2,745 per tonne on a C&F basis, U.S. and Canadian knuckle was bought at $2,540 a tonne and their short-rib at $3,600-$3,955 a tonne, traders said.
Australian grass-fed fullset beef was bought at between $2,515-$2,586 a tonne and Australian and New Zealand grass-fed bone-in beef at between $1,699-$1,741, they said.
Arrivals were set for Seoul (6,557 tonnes), Pusan (886 tonnes), Taegu (144 tonnes) and Naju (508 tonnes).
Shipments of 4,061 tonnes were slated for July 25 and 4,034 tonnes for August 5.
